key_insight: Two finite-element discretisations preserve entropy generation and pointwise quasi-incompressibility in thermal multicomponent flows, with the continuous Petrov–Galerkin method also conserving total energy.
engineering_relevance: These methods support physically consistent simulation of miscible mixtures with coupled diffusion, heat transfer and fluid motion.
method: Formulate the thermal Maxwell–Stefan–Navier–Stokes system using an entropy balance.
Combine semi-implicit Euler time stepping with suitable finite elements; total energy is numerically dissipated.
Use continuous Petrov–Galerkin time discretisation to conserve total energy and enable high-order time approximations.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments demonstrate the structure-preserving properties and behaviour of both methods, but the abstract provides no quantitative error or runtime results.
watch_item: The semi-implicit Euler method introduces numerical energy dissipation, which may matter when energy conservation is critical.
paper_title: Structure-preserving discretisations for the quasi-incompressible, thermal Maxwell-Stefan equations
